text: {"observations":"In the 0-2 kHz zoom, the voiced segments show clearly separated harmonics spaced roughly 200-250 Hz apart (e.g. near the start and around 5.8-6.3 s), which puts the fundamental at about 200-250 Hz. That is too high for a typical adult man (around 100-130 Hz), which rules out C, and is lower than a typical young child (often 300 Hz or more), which makes A less likely. The 0-8 kHz view shows adult-like formant structure and fluent, rapid syllable rate, with strong fricative energy up to 8 kHz. A teenager cannot be excluded on pitch alone, but an adult female voice is the best fit, so B.","answer":"B"}
